sentences.l: hail · to-face · your · gods · these
sentences.i: Hail to you, you gods here!
sentences.n: ind ḥr·ṯn is the greeting 'hail to you': ind is the reed i, the sign nḏ (an uncertain object, perhaps a spindle) with the cobra ḏ as its complement, and the papyrus roll as classifier — it grew from i 'O' and nḏ ḥr 'greet the face'. ḥr 'face' is the face with stroke (a second stroke follows it), and ·ṯn 'your' (plural, for the gods are many) is written here in its older form, tethering-rope ṯ, water n and plural strokes; elsewhere in this text it is loaf t, n and strokes, ·tn. nṯrw 'gods' is the flag nṯr three times, and ipw 'these' (reed i, stool p, quail chick w, stroke) is the plural demonstrative, pointing at the gods present. The address is supplied by Budge from Naville's text of other papyri, where the dead man goes on to speak to the gods of the hall after the 42 declarations.

sentences.l: I · know · I · you · know · I · names · your
sentences.i: I know you; I know your names.
sentences.n: iw·i (reed i, quail chick w, seated man ·i) opens the statement: 'I'. rḫ·kwi is the stative of rḫ 'know' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, the papyrus roll for an abstract) with the 1st-person ending ·kwi, written here k, a stroke and w (the print sets the stroke and the chick side by side, so the order of the two is not meaningful); the stative of rḫ means 'I know', the knowledge being a state. Budge prints rḫ·kwi and the following tn as one group; they are split here, for tn (loaf t, water n, plural strokes) is a word of its own, the dependent pronoun 'you' (plural), object of the verb. The second rḫ·kwi has the same spelling with chick and stroke in the usual order. rn 'name' (mouth r, water n) is followed by a man with his hand to his mouth, which the print gives where a name-classifier might stand, and a stroke; no plural is written, but the gods are many and 'your names' is meant. To know a being's name is to have power over it: the claim opens the plea.

sentences.l: not · fall · I · to · slaughter · your
sentences.i: I shall not fall to your slaughter.
sentences.n: nn (water n written twice) is the negative of the future: nn + sḏm·f, 'I shall not …'. ḫr·i is ḫr 'fall' (placenta ḫ, mouth r) with ·i; its classifier is printed as a cord with crossing ends (coded V12), not the falling man the verb usually takes, and the sign is doubtful. n is the preposition 'to'. šꜥt 'slaughter, the slaughtering' is pool š (the print's sign is an approximation), arm ꜥ and loaf t, with a spiky sign (coded M44, approximate) and the knife as classifiers and plural strokes; then ·tn 'your'. The gods of the hall are executioners as well as judges.

sentences.l: not · report · you · evil · my · to · god · this · who · you · in-the-following · his
sentences.i: You will not report my wrong to this god whom you follow.
sentences.n: Another nn + sḏm·f: 'you will not …'. sꜥr is the causative of ꜥr 'go up': 'make go up', that is, bring a matter up to a superior, report it; it is the folded cloth s, arm ꜥ and mouth r, with a sign the print gives like a balance (coded U38, approximate) — fitting for a report that is to be weighed. The text writes b-i with the sparrow; read bin 'evil, wrong': the n is left out (Budge restores it in his transliteration but nothing stands for it in the signs). ·i 'my'. n nṯr pn 'to this god': pn 'this' (stool p, water n) follows its noun. nty ṯn m-ḫt·f 'whom you follow', literally 'who you (are) in his following': nty is the relative 'who', ṯn the dependent pronoun 'you' in its older spelling with ṯ, and m-ḫt 'after, in the train of' is owl m, the tree ḫt with ḫ and t as complements and the walking legs, + ·f. 'This god' is presumably the judge of the hall.

sentences.l: not · come · case · my · before · you
sentences.i: My case will not come before you.
sentences.n: nn again, with iw 'come' (the walking legs as word-sign with w as complement, as in the introduction). A loaf t follows the verb, and it is not clear what it is: if nn stands here for the single n, as later copies often write it, iwt would be the sḏmt·f, 'my case has not yet come before you'; it could also be a slip for the impersonal ·tw. It is translated with nn as written, as the future. sp 'occasion, case' (bolt s, stool p) here means a deed charged against the speaker; its classifier is printed as the sun-disc, not the threshing-floor sp normally takes (and has on line 6), and the word is read sp either way. ḥr·tn 'before you, to you' is the face ḥr with r as complement and ·tn.

sentences.l: speak · you · truth · about · me · before · the-hand · of-the-Lord-to-the-Limit
sentences.i: You shall speak the truth about me in the presence of the Lord of All.
sentences.n: ḏd·tn 'you shall speak' (cobra ḏ, hand d, ·tn) is the sḏm·f used as a wish or instruction. mꜣꜥt 'truth, right' is spelled out here: sickle mꜣ, arm ꜥ, loaf t, with the plinth mꜣꜥ, papyrus roll and plural strokes after it as classifiers. r·i 'concerning me'. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is owl m and the phallus sign bꜣḥ with stroke and papyrus roll. ꜥ 'hand' (the arm with its stroke) then stands between m-bꜣḥ and the god's name; 'before the hand of' is what the signs say, a way of naming the god's power. nb-r-ḏr 'the Lord to the Limit' (basket nb, mouth r, the plant ḏr with r as its complement, seated god) is the creator, lord of everything there is.

sentences.l: because · have-done · I · truth · in · Egypt
sentences.i: For I have done what is right in Egypt.
sentences.n: ḥr-ntt 'because' is the preposition ḥr 'on account of' (the face with its stroke) and ntt 'that' (water n, two loaves t). Budge prints it as two groups with one gloss; it is one word here. ir·n·i is the sḏm·n·f of iri 'do': the eye ir, then the n that marks the completed action, then ·i: 'I did, I have done'. mꜣꜥt as on line 5. tꜣ-mri 'Egypt' is the land sign tꜣ, a hoe for mr (the print gives it with a different hoe-shape, coded U6), reed i, and a stalk-shaped sign and the town sign as classifiers.

sentences.l: not · reviled(?) · I · god · not · came · case · my
sentences.i: I have not reviled(?) the god; no case of mine has come (before you).
sentences.n: n with a sḏm·f is the past negative: 'I did not, I have not'. Here it is written with the water n, not the arms D35 of the declarations. The verb is the lasso-sign šn with water n, a man with his hand to his mouth (speech) and ·i; Budge gives 'curse', and a verb of evil speech is what the classifier suggests, but no verb šn of this sense is well attested and the reading is doubtful (it may stand for šnṯ 'revile'). n iw sp·i: 'my case has not come', with iw written as on line 5 but without the t; sp here has its proper classifier, the threshing-floor.

sentences.l: hail · to-face · your · gods · who-are-in · hall · your · of · the-Two-Truths · without(?) · falsehood · in · bodies · their
sentences.i: Hail to you, you gods who are in your Hall of the Two Truths, who have no falsehood in their bodies,
sentences.n: The greeting of line 2 again, now with ·tn written loaf t, water n, plural strokes. The text writes reed i with the crossed planks im; read imyw 'who are in' (the nisba of m 'in'), its plural ending not written. wsḫt 'hall' is quail chick w (ahead of its sign), the cup wsḫ, loaf t and the house as classifier, with ·ṯn 'your' in the older spelling (no ḫ is written beside the cup). nt 'of' (n + t) is the feminine genitive, agreeing with wsḫt; mꜣꜥti 'the Two Truths' is sickle, arm, loaf t, two strokes y and the feather of Maat twice. The text writes water n, t, vulture ꜣ, the sparrow and plural strokes; read iwty 'who have no …', the negative relative (Budge: àt 'without'). On line 18 the same word is written with the spread arms (D35) for iwt, t, the vulture standing for -y and the sparrow; here the water n stands in for the arms, which are also read n. The reading is probable, not certain. The text writes g-r; read grg 'falsehood, lie': the second g is not written, unless the stick-sign that follows (coded T14, approximate) stands for it. ẖt·sn 'their bodies': ẖt 'belly, body' is the belly-and-teats sign ẖ with t and strokes, then ·sn 'their' (bolt s, water n, strokes).

morph.gloss: falsehood, lie (noun; from grg "tell lies")

sentences.l: who-live · on · truth · in · Heliopolis · who-swallow · of · innards(?) · their · before · Horus · who-is-in · disk · his
sentences.i: who live on truth in Heliopolis, who swallow their innards(?) in the presence of Horus who is in his disk:
sentences.n: ꜥnḫyw 'who live' is the plural participle of ꜥnḫ: the ankh-sign ꜥnḫ, two reeds y, quail chick w and stroke. ꜥnḫ m 'live on' (food): the gods feed on truth (mꜣꜥt spelled out as on line 5). iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn, the pot nw and the town sign. sꜥmyw 'who swallow' (bolt s, arm ꜥ, owl m, two reeds y, chick w) is another plural participle; sꜥm is 'swallow, gulp down', and its classifiers are a horned head on a pole (coded F1, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth, for eating. sꜥm m is 'swallow (some) of'. What they swallow is doubtful: ḥꜣwt (the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ, t, w) has the coiled intestine (coded F46, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, so 'innards' is meant, + ·sn 'their'; Budge's 'entrails' rests on the same sign. Whose innards — the gods' own, or the wicked's — the text does not say. m-bꜣḥ as on line 5. Horus is the falcon with the seated god; imy 'who is in' (reed i, crossed planks im), and itn·f 'his disk' (i, t, n, the sun-disc, ·f): the sun's disk, here Horus as the sun.

morph.gloss: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru)

sentences.l: rescue · you · me · from · Babi · who-lives · on · entrails · of-officials · day · that · of · reckoning · great · in-the-hand-of · you
sentences.i: Rescue me from Babi, who lives on the entrails of officials, on that day of the great reckoning that is in your hands.
sentences.n: nḥm 'take away' — of a person, 'rescue, save' — is water n, the bowl ḥm (scalloped in the print) with owl m as complement and a classifier of force (coded U15), then ·tn 'you'. Budge prints one group nḥm·tn·wi; it is split here, for the last two signs, stroke and quail chick w, are the dependent pronoun wi 'me' (the stroke standing where the seated man of 'I, me' would be), the object. nḥm·tn is the sḏm·f as an entreaty: 'may you rescue'. m-ꜥ 'from (the hand of)' is owl m over the arm ꜥ (printed as a ligature). bꜣby 'Babi' is b, ꜣ, ꜣ, b and two reeds y with the seated god: the doubled vulture is the print's, read once. ꜥnḫ m 'who lives on' (ankh with n and ḫ as complements). bskw 'entrails' (b, s, k, the intestine, w and stroke). srw 'officials, magnates' is the standing official with a staff (coded A21) with w, the seated man and stroke. hrw pwy 'that day' (the sun-disc and stroke for hrw; pwy is stool p, chick w, two reeds y). ipt 'reckoning, assessment' (reed i, stool p, loaf t, papyrus roll) from ip 'count'; ꜥꜣt 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ with ꜥ, the feminine t, and the roll. m-ꜥ·tn 'with you, in your hands' closes the clause. Babi is a savage baboon-god, a devourer of the condemned.

morph.gloss: day (noun)
great (adjective)

sentences.l: have-come · I · to · you
sentences.i: I have come to you.
sentences.n: ii·kwi is the stative of ii 'come' with ·kwi (reed-leaf ii, reed i as complement, walking legs, then k, w and stroke): 'I have come', the arrival seen as a state. ḫr 'to, near' (placenta ḫ, mouth r) is the preposition used of going to a person, + ·tn.

morph.gloss: to, near, with (preposition; of persons)

sentences.l: not · wrong · my · not · crime · my · not · evil · my · not · witness · my · not · did · I · thing · against · him
sentences.i: There is no wrong in me, no crime in me, no evil in me; no witness speaks against me(?); there is no one against whom I have done anything.
sentences.n: nn + noun is 'there is not': nn isft·i 'there is no wrong of mine' (isft, the word of the declarations: reed i, s, f, t, the sparrow for something bad, stroke, ·i). ḫbnt 'crime, guilt' is placenta ḫ, b, n, t with the crossed sticks and the sparrow, + ·i. The third clause has a single n, read as the same negative. ḏw 'evil' is the mountain ḏw (the same word as 'mountain') with w, the sparrow and strokes, + ·i. mtrw 'witness' (the phallus mt, t, r, w, two strokes, the man with hand to mouth) + ·i: 'there is no witness of mine' is taken to mean no witness who could speak against me; the sense is not certain. nn ir·n·i ḫt r·f, literally 'there is not (one) — I did a thing against him': nn followed by a whole clause. ḫt 'thing' (ḫ, t, roll, strokes); r·f 'against him'. If nn stands here for the single n of the past, as the note on line 5 allows, the clause is simply 'I have not done anything against him', 'him' being the god; either way the sense is that he has wronged no one.

sentences.l: live · I · on · truth · swallow · I · of · truth · of-heart · my
sentences.i: I live on truth; I swallow the truth of my heart.
sentences.n: ꜥnḫ·i m mꜣꜥt 'I live on truth': the sḏm·f, here a general statement. The speaker claims what was said of the gods on line 7. mꜣꜥt is spelled with the feather of Maat as classifier this time. sꜥm·i 'I swallow' (bolt s, arm ꜥ, owl m, the horned head on a pole (coded F1, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth, ·i). ib·i 'my heart' is the heart-jar ib with stroke; the suffix ·i is in square brackets in Budge's line, his restoration of damage. mꜣꜥt ib·i, 'the truth of my heart', is a direct genitive.

sentences.l: did · I · what-say · people · what-are-pleased · the-gods · with-it
sentences.i: I have done what people say is right, and what the gods are pleased with.
sentences.n: iw ir·n·i: the particle iw (here with no suffix; the subject is in the ·i of the verb) and the sḏm·n·f 'I have done'. ḏdt (cobra ḏ, hand d, t, strokes) is the relative form 'what (people) say' — that is, what people hold to be right. rmṯ 'people' is written r-t with the seated man, the seated woman and stroke as classifiers: the m of rmṯ is not written and the loaf t stands for ṯ, a shortened spelling of the later papyri. hrrt (h, r, r, t, roll) is the relative form of hri 'be content, pleased': 'that which the gods are pleased with', the ḥr·s 'with it' at the end picking up the relative. ·s 'it' (the folded cloth s) is the feminine suffix, used for a neuter 'it'.

sentences.l: satisfied · I · god · with · what-desires · he
sentences.i: I have satisfied the god with what he desires.
sentences.n: sḥtp is the causative of ḥtp 'be content': 'make content, satisfy, appease'. It is the folded cloth s, the offering-table ḥtp with t and p as complements, then the n of the sḏm·n·f. The suffix after it is written quail chick w and stroke, as in the dependent pronoun wi; read ·i, 'I have satisfied'. nṯr is the flag with the seated god. mrt·f 'what he desires' is the hoe mr with r, t, the man with hand to mouth, stroke and ·f — the relative form of mri 'love, wish', with only one r written. Budge prints the line-numeral 11 inside this word, between the stroke and ·f.

sentences.l: gave · I · bread · to · the-hungry · water · to · the-thirsty · clothes · to · the-naked · ferry-boat · (to) · the-boatless
sentences.i: I have given bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked, and a ferry-boat to one who had no boat.
sentences.n: rdi·n·i 'I have given' (mouth r, the arm giving di — printed without its loaf — the n of the past, ·i). t 'bread' is the loaf t with a long loaf and a cup holding a cone of bread (coded W10, approximate) as classifiers, and strokes. n 'to'. The text writes ḥ-q-t; read ḥqr 'hungry': the r is written as t, a slip, and 'bread to the hungry' allows no other reading (wick ḥ, triangle q, the sparrow and strokes as classifiers). mw 'water' is the three ripples alone. The next n 'to' is the Red Crown, which reads n. iby 'thirsty' is reed i, foot b and the leaping kid ib, with two strokes y, water and the man with hand to mouth (for drinking). ḥbsw 'clothes' (wick ḥ, foot b, cloth s, w, a fringed cloth as classifier). ḥꜣyw 'the naked' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ, two strokes y and w, the fringed cloth and a man. mḫnt 'ferry-boat' is owl m over the arm (the ligature that writes m in later spellings), an animal sign that stands for ḫn (coded E14, approximate; the same sign appears in ẖnw on line 15), water n and a boat, the feminine t unwritten; Budge's 'and a boat' takes the owl as 'and'. No n 'to' is written before the last word. iwy 'boatless' is the young animal iw, w, two strokes y, the boat and a man. The four gifts are the stock good deeds of an Egyptian life.

sentences.l: made · I · god's-offerings · for · the-gods · invocation-offerings · for · the-spirits
sentences.i: I have made god's offerings for the gods and invocation-offerings for the spirits.
sentences.n: ḥtp-nṯr 'god's offerings' is written with the flag nṯr first, in honour of the god, then the offering-table ḥtp with t and p, a loaf and strokes; Budge reads it in the written order (neter-ḥetepu). prt-ḫrw, the invocation-offering — literally 'the going forth of the voice', food called into being by the spoken formula — is the house pr with the oar ḫrw printed inside it, a loaf and strokes. ꜣḫw 'spirits' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, w and a seated figure holding something before him (coded A51, approximate). Gods receive temple offerings, the blessed dead the offering-formula.

sentences.l: rescue · you · me · then · you · protect · me · then · you
sentences.i: Rescue me, then; protect me, then!
sentences.n: nḥm·tn wi as on line 8 (here wi is quail chick w and the seated man). ir·tn is r 'to' with ·tn, the construction that follows a command to strengthen it: 'you, then'. Budge prints ir and tn as two groups; they are joined here as one word. ḫw 'protect', with no suffix, is the imperative: placenta ḫ with a low hooked sign under it (coded S45, approximate; its value is not clear and it is taken as classifier), w, the papyrus roll and stroke; it is followed by wi 'me' (chick w and seated man), which Budge prints in the same group and which is split off here.

sentences.l: not · report · you · against · me · before · god · great
sentences.i: You will not accuse me before the great god.
sentences.n: nn + sḏm·f, the future negative again. smi 'report, accuse' is the folded cloth s, the milk-jug in its net mi with reed i as complement, and the man with hand to mouth; smi r is 'report against, accuse'. Then ·tn, r·i 'against me', m-bꜣḥ, and nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god', the flag and the column ꜥꜣ. The great god is presumably Osiris, before whom the judgement is held.

morph.gloss: great (adjective)

sentences.l: I · pure · of-mouth · pure · of-hands
sentences.i: I am pure of mouth and pure of hands.
sentences.n: ink 'I' (the pot nw for in, basket k, seated man), the independent pronoun, with wꜥb used as a noun, 'a pure one': 'I am one pure of …'. wꜥb 'pure' is a single sign, a jar pouring water over a foot — washing. rꜣ 'mouth' (mouth with stroke) and ꜥwy 'the two hands' (two arms, two strokes y and w) follow it directly: 'pure of mouth, pure of hands', clean in speech and deed.

sentences.l: is-said · to-him · welcome · twice · by · those-who-see · him
sentences.i: Those who see him say to him, "Welcome, welcome!"
sentences.n: ḏd·tw 'one says, it is said': ḏd with the impersonal suffix ·tw (loaf t, chick w). Budge prints ḏd·tw and n·f 'to him' as one group; they are split here. n·f is the preposition n with ·f: the text now speaks of the dead man in the third person. iy wy 'how welcome!': iy 'come' (reed-leaf ii, two strokes y, walking legs) with the particle wy (chick w, two strokes y) that exclaims over a quality — 'how come (you are)!'. sp sn, the threshing-floor sp and the numeral 2, means 'twice': the word before it is to be said twice. in 'by' names the speakers: mꜣꜣyw 'those who see' (sickle mꜣ, the eye, vulture ꜣ, two reeds y, chick w, stroke), the plural participle of mꜣꜣ, with sw 'him' (the sedge sw with w), the dependent pronoun as object.

sentences.l: because · heard · I · word · that · spoken-by · the-donkey · with · the-cat · in · the-house · of-Heped-ra(?)
sentences.i: For I heard that word which the donkey spoke with the cat in the house of Heped-ra(?).
sentences.n: The dead man speaks again. ḥr-ntt 'because', as on line 6. sḏm·n·i 'I heard' is the ear sḏm with owl m as complement, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. The printed signs are the staff md, hand d, t, the man with hand to mouth and stroke: mdt 'word, speech' (Budge's transliteration, t'eṭet, does not match them). twy 'that' (t, w, two reeds) is the feminine demonstrative, agreeing with mdt. ḏdt (cobra ḏ, hand d, t) is the relative form 'which … spoke', and its subject follows directly: 'which the donkey spoke'; Budge's transliteration line adds a word 'by' with no sign above it, and nothing is read for it. ꜥꜣ 'donkey' is the column ꜥꜣ with the donkey as classifier; between them stands the phallus-like sign of m-bꜣḥ, which has no evident part in the word and is taken as a second classifier. ḥnꜥ 'with' (wick ḥ, water n, arm ꜥ); miw 'cat' (the milk-jug mi with i, w, the cat). pr 'house' with its stroke. The god's name is wick ḥ, stool p, hand d, the crossed sticks, mouth r with stroke and the seated god; read ḥpd-rꜣ, perhaps 'Open of Mouth' (ḥpd 'open (the mouth)' + rꜣ 'mouth'), but the name is not known elsewhere and its reading is uncertain. What the donkey and the cat said is not told; it was a word the speaker could repeat, and so a proof that he had been there.

morph.gloss: donkey, ass (noun)

sentences.l: witnessed · I · in · face · his · gave · he · judgement(?)
sentences.i: I bore witness before him, and he gave judgement(?).
sentences.n: mtrw·i has the same signs as on line 9 (the phallus mt, t, r, w, two strokes, the man with hand to mouth, ·i), here the verb 'bear witness' in the sḏm·f, told of the past; there is no n of the sḏm·n·f, and the sense 'I bore witness' is taken from what follows. Who 'he' is — the god of the house, or the judge — is not said. m ḥr·f 'before him', literally 'in his face' (the face with its stroke, r, ·f). di·f 'he gave' (the giving arm, here with its loaf, + ·f). The last word is doubtful: its first sign is printed unclearly and is coded as the sign wḏꜥ 'judge' (approximate), followed by w, t, the man with hand to mouth, stroke and the seated god; read wḏꜥwt 'judgement, decision'. Budge reads a different word (tentu) with the same sense.

sentences.l: saw · I · the-splitting · of-the-persea · in · the-interior · of-Rosetau
sentences.i: I have seen the splitting of the persea tree within Rosetau.
sentences.n: iw mꜣꜣ·n·i 'I have seen': the eye and sickle printed as a ligature (eye first, as in the introduction), the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. psš 'splitting, division' is stool p, bolt s and the pool š (approximate), with the crossed sticks and a low sign (coded U15) as classifiers. išd 'persea tree' is reed i, a sign coded as šd (approximate) with hand d as complement, and the tree. m ẖnw 'within, inside' (ẖnw 'interior': the animal sign of mḫnt on line 11 standing for ẖn, approximate, water n, pot nw, w and the house). rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau', the realm of the dead near Giza, is mouth rꜣ with stroke, the hanging spiral sṯꜣ with two strokes, and the hills. The persea was the sacred tree of Heliopolis; what its splitting at Rosetau was is not told here.

sentences.l: I · report · I · before · the-gods · knowing · what-concerns · bodies · their
sentences.i: As for me, I make my report before the gods, knowing what concerns their persons.
sentences.n: Here a new address begins in Naville's text. ink 'I' is the independent pronoun: the nw-pot (in), the basket (k) and the seated man as classifier. It stands at the head of the sentence for emphasis, 'I, I …'. smi·i 'I report' is from smi 'report, make petition'. The signs are the folded cloth s; a sign printed as three reeds on a slab (coded M20, approximate), standing for sm; the owl m as complement; two strokes for i; a w; the man with his hand to his mouth (speech); and ·i, the seated man, 'I', the 1st person suffix. The w has no place in the verb form, and with it the group could also be the noun 'my reports'. The second sign is not secure either. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is the owl m with the phallus sign bꜣḥ and its stroke. nṯrw 'gods' writes the god's flag three times for the plural. rḫ 'knowing' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, papyrus roll) has no ending and is taken as describing the speaker. ẖrt 'what belongs to, concerns' is the butcher's block ẖr with r, t and two classifiers. ẖt 'body' (the belly sign ẖ with t) here means the gods' persons. ·sn 'their', the 3rd person plural suffix, is the bolt s with water n and plural strokes.

sentences.l: have-come · I · here · to · testify-to · truth
sentences.i: I have come here to bear witness to what is right.
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the sḏm·n·f, the form for a completed action. It is the verb ii (the reed-leaf ii, a reed i and the walking legs), then the n that marks the form, then ·i. ꜥꜣ, the column, is read as the adverb 'here, hither', as in the introduction's ii·n·i ꜥꜣ. Under it the print sets the same balance-like sign as in sꜥr on line 4 (coded U38, approximate). It has no clear place here and is taken as a classifier, so the reading is doubtful (Budge: 'advancing'). r + infinitive gives the purpose. smtr is the bolt s, the phallus sign mt, t, mouth r, two strokes and the man with his hand to his mouth. It is the causative of mtr 'bear witness', 'examine, testify', and the two strokes are not read. mꜣꜥt, Maat, 'what is right, truth', is written here with sickle mꜣ, arm ꜥ, t, the papyrus roll and a stroke, without the plinth.

sentences.l: to · set · the-balance · upon · stands · its · in · the-interior · of-the-gaiu-plants(?)
sentences.i: and to set the balance upon its stands within the gaiu-plants(?).
sentences.n: A second purpose clause. rdit 'to set' is the infinitive of rdi 'give, put': mouth r, the giving arm di (printed without its loaf), and the t of the infinitive. iwsw 'balance' is the young animal iw with w, the sedge sw with w again, and the balance itself as classifier. ꜥḥꜥw is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with ꜥ, w, walking legs and plural strokes, from ꜥḥꜥ 'stand': 'stands, supports'. ·f 'its' is the horned viper. m ẖnw 'within' is m with ẖnw 'interior'. The print writes ẖnw with a quadruped (coded E14, approximate) where the usual sign is expected, then n, the nw-pot, w and a house. gꜣiw (jar-stand g, vulture ꜣ, reed i, w, a flowering plant and plural strokes) names some plants or a thicket, and what it is is not known (Budge: 'amaranthine bushes'). The balance is the scales of the judgement.

sentences.l: O · High-one · upon · standard · his · lord · of-the-atef-crown · who-made · name · his · as · lord · of-breath
sentences.i: O High One upon his standard, lord of the atef-crown, who has made his name as Lord of Breath:
sentences.n: A new address, now to a single god. i 'O' is the reed with the man with his hand to his mouth (a call). qꜣ 'high' (hill-slope q, vulture ꜣ, a man with raised arms, papyrus roll) is used as a noun, 'High One'. ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. iꜣt 'standard' is the pole on which a god's emblem stands: reed i, vulture ꜣ, t, the standard itself and a seated god. ·f 'his'. nb 'lord' is the basket. ꜣtf (vulture ꜣ, t, f, w and the crown) is the atef, the tall plumed crown of Osiris. iri 'who made' is the eye ir with two reeds, a participle. rn·f 'his name'. nfw 'breath, wind' is the sail (coded P5, approximate) with w, a stroke and a seated god. Budge reads it nifu; the sail can also be read ṯꜣw, another word for 'wind, breath'. The god is not named, but the titles suit Osiris.

sentences.l: saved · I · from · those-of-yours · of · messengers · who-inflict · harm · who-bring-about · punishments(?) · without · covering · of · faces · their
sentences.i: May I be saved from those messengers of yours who inflict harm and bring about punishments(?), whose faces are uncovered,
sentences.n: nḥm 'take away, rescue' is water n, the bowl ḥm with m as complement, and the low sign printed U15 for the forearm with stick, the classifier of force. Here it carries ·kwi (k, w and the seated man), the ending of the stative for 'I': 'I am saved'. The stative is now and then used for a wish (most often in the 2nd person), and 'may I be saved' is taken so here; Budge takes it as a command, 'deliver me'. m-ꜥ 'from (the hand of)' is the owl m joined to the arm ꜥ. nꜣy·k (water n, vulture ꜣ, two reeds, plural strokes, the basket ·k) is the possessive article of later Egyptian, 'your'. The n after it is the genitive 'of' and is not needed in English. wpwtyw 'messengers' is the horns wp (coded F13, approximate) with p, w and t, then the vulture standing for the ending -y as in ḫftyw, crossed sticks, a second t, the papyrus roll and plural strokes. wddyw (w, two hands d, two reeds, crossed sticks, w, stroke) is read as the imperfective participle of wdi 'put, cast, inflict' (the doubled d is its gemination), which is not certain. ṯmsw 'harm, injuries' is the tethering rope ṯ and the fox-skins ms with s and w, then classifiers including the bad bird. It is a rare word, and the identifications of its first sign and classifiers are approximate. sḫpryw 'who bring about' is the causative of ḫpr 'come into being': s, the scarab ḫpr, r, two reeds, stroke and w. idryt (reed i, hand d, mouth r, two reeds, t, a plant coded M2 (approximate) and the papyrus roll) is not otherwise known to this edition. 'Punishments, afflictions' follows the sense and Budge's 'calamities'. iwty 'who has not, without' is the negative relative: the spread arms (D35), t, the vulture for -y and the bad bird. ṯꜣmt 'covering, veil' is the duckling ṯꜣ with ꜣ, m, t, a fringed cloth (approximate) and the U15 sign. nt is the feminine form of the genitive, agreeing with it. ḥrw·sn 'their faces' is the face with two strokes and ·sn.

morph.gloss: to rescue, save (from) (verb; the same word as nḥm "take away")

sentences.l: because · have-done · I · truth · lord · of-Maat
sentences.i: because I have done what is right, O Lord of Maat.
sentences.n: ḥr-ntt 'because' (as on line 6) is ḥr 'upon' (face and stroke) with ntt 'that', the feminine of nty (water n, t, t). Budge prints it as two sign groups with one gloss; here it is one word. ir·n·i 'I have done' is the eye ir, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. In the first mꜣꜥt the plinth comes after the t as a further classifier. nb mꜣꜥt has a seated god after the basket. No n 'for' stands before it, so it is taken as a call, 'O Lord of Maat', not 'for the Lord of Maat'.

sentences.l: pure · I · breast · my · in · purification · hinder-parts · my · cleansed · inside · my · in · the-pool · of-Maat
sentences.i: I am pure: my breast is in purification, my hinder parts are cleansed, and my inner parts are in the pool of Maat.
sentences.n: wꜥb 'pure' is the sign of a foot under a stream of water poured from a jar (coded D60), with the water ripples. ·kwi (k, a stroke for i, w) is the stative ending for 'I': 'I am pure'. ḥꜣty 'breast, heart' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t, two strokes y and the heart as classifier; ·i 'my'. ꜥbw 'purification' is arm ꜥ, foot b, w, a pouring vessel (coded W15, approximate) and water. pḥwy 'hinder parts, back' is the lion's hindquarters pḥ, two reeds and a flesh classifier (approximate). twri 'cleansed' (t, the swallow wr with r, reed i, a pouring sign and the papyrus roll) is from twr 'be clean, purify' and is taken as a stative. ḥry-ib, 'what is upon the heart', usually 'midst', is written face ḥr, r and heart ib without its y. Here it is the inside of the body. šdyt 'pool, basin' is the waterskin šd (F30) with d, two reeds, t and a canal classifier (coded N23, approximate); this is Budge's seśeṭit. Part by part the speaker declares his body washed clean.

morph.gloss: midst; the inside, inner parts (of the body) (noun; lit. "what is upon the heart")

sentences.l: not-is · a-limb · in · me · empty
sentences.i: There is no limb in me that is lacking.
sentences.n: nn (water n twice) denies existence: 'there is not'. ꜥt 'limb, member' is arm ꜥ, t and a flesh classifier (coded F51, approximate). im·i is m 'in' with ·i; m becomes im before a suffix. šw 'empty, lacking, free of' is the feather šw with w and the bad bird. The text does not say what the limb would lack: Maat, or the cleansing just named.

sentences.l: purified · I · in · the-pool · southern · rested · I · in · Hemet · northern · in · the-field · of-grasshoppers
sentences.i: I have purified myself in the southern pool, and I have rested in northern Hemet, in the Field of the Grasshoppers.
sentences.n: wꜥb·n·i 'I have purified (myself)' is the sḏm·n·f of wꜥb. rsyt 'southern' is the plant of the south rs with t. The small slanted sign after rs (coded M44, approximate) carries no sound; it comes again in sḫt below. ḥtp·n·i 'I have rested' is the offering table ḥtp with t and p, then n and ·i. ḥmt (the bowl ḥm, m, t) has the town sign, so it is a place, Hemet, not otherwise known here. It is spelled like ḥmt 'woman'. mḥtt 'north' is the whip-like sign mḥ with t, t and a canal classifier (approximate). It is taken as the adjective 'northern', agreeing with Hemet and answering 'southern' with the pool. Budge reads 'to the north of the field', which leaves the m before sḫt unexplained. sḫt 'field' is a field of reeds (coded M20, approximate) with a stroke, the small slanted sign and t. snḥmw 'grasshoppers, locusts' is s (a duck coded G39, approximate), n, the bowl ḥm with m, w and the grasshopper itself.

morph.gloss: Hemet, a place in the world below, written with the town sign (not otherwise known; Budge: Hemet)
field, marshland (noun; sḫt snḥmw "the Field of the Grasshoppers")

sentences.l: which-bathe · the-Qedty(?) · in · it · at · the-hour · of-night · for · smoothing · the-heart · of · the-gods
sentences.i: in which the Qedty(?) bathe at the hour of night, to soothe the heart of the gods.
sentences.n: The sentence goes on. wꜥbt is wꜥb 'be pure, cleanse oneself, bathe' (the foot under water) with t and water. It is taken as the relative form, feminine to agree with the Field: 'in which … bathe'. im·s 'in it' is m with ·s, the 3rd person feminine suffix (here the bolt), which points back to the Field. qdty is the builder's level qd (coded Aa28, approximate), t, two strokes and two seated gods. It names a pair or group of divine beings not otherwise known here (Budge: 'the divine sailors'). In m wnwt grḥ 'at the hour of night', wnwt 'hour' is the hare wn with n, a star, the nw-pot, t and the sun. grḥ 'night' is jar-stand g, r, ḥ, a sky sign with a hanging star (coded N2, approximate) and the sun. n snꜥꜥ is n 'for' with the infinitive of snꜥꜥ 'make smooth' (s, n, two arms ꜥ, a scribe's kit and the papyrus roll). snꜥꜥ ib, 'smooth the heart', is to soothe or please; Budge queries the word.

sentences.l: after · passed · I · by · it · by · night · by · day
sentences.i: after I have passed by it, by night and by day.
sentences.n: m-ḫt 'after' is the owl m and the branch ḫt, with ḫ, walking legs and t. Before a verb it means 'after (someone) has …'. swꜣ 'pass by' is the crossed sticks with the walking legs. Budge reads the group seś, but crossed sticks with legs is the usual writing of swꜣ, and swꜣ ḥr is 'pass by'. ·i 'I'. ḥr·s 'by it' is ḥr (face, r) with ·s, the folded cloth, again the Field. m grḥ m hrw 'by night and by day': grḥ here has no sun sign, and hrw 'day' is the sun with its stroke. Where this clause belongs is not certain: it may close the sentence before or lead into the questioning that follows.

morph.gloss: day (noun; the sun sign with its stroke)

sentences.l: let · coming · his · say · they · to · me
sentences.i: 'Let him come,' they say to me.
sentences.n: The gods now speak, and the questioning begins. di is the giving arm (with its loaf) and plural strokes. It is rdi 'give, let', and its object is iwt·f 'his coming': walking legs iw, w, the t of the infinitive and ·f. Together they mean 'let him come'. The strokes may mark a passive ('his coming is granted') or the plural of the speakers; Budge has 'they grant his coming'. in·sn 'they say' is the verb in 'say' (reed i, water n), normally used only after the words quoted, with ·sn. r·i 'to me' is r with ·i. The gods speak of the newcomer as 'him' while addressing him.

morph.gloss: say, said (verb; only after the words quoted: in·sn "they say")

sentences.l: who · then · you · say · they · to · me
sentences.i: 'Who are you, then?' they say to me.
sentences.n: nym 'who?' is water n with the owl-and-arm ligature, in which the arm is not read (as in m-ꜥ). tr is t, r, a knotted stalk (coded M6) and the man with his hand to his mouth. It is the particle 'then, pray' that presses a question. tw (t, w) 'you' is the dependent pronoun of the 2nd person singular, the subject after the question word.

morph.gloss: say, said (verb; only after the words quoted: in·sn "they say")

sentences.l: what · then · name · your · say · they · to · me
sentences.i: 'What, then, is your name?' they say to me.
sentences.n: pw (stool p, quail chick w) is here the question word 'who? what?', again pressed by tr, which this time has a reed i in its writing. rn·k 'your name' is mouth r, water n, the man with his hand to his mouth, and ·k, the basket, 'your'. As at the door in the introduction, the gods ask for a name.

morph.gloss: say, said (verb; only after the words quoted: in·sn "they say")

sentences.l: I (am) · who-grows · beneath · of · the-thicket(?) · who-is-in · the-moringa · name · my
sentences.i: 'I am He-who-grows-beneath-the-thicket(?), He-who-is-in-the-moringa-tree: (that is) my name.'
sentences.n: The speaker answers with names. ink 'I' is written without the seated man this time; ink + noun is 'I am …'. rd 'grow' is mouth r and hand d before the bowstring rd (coded T12, approximate). It is spelled like rd 'foot' but is the verb, here a participle 'who grows'. ẖry 'who is beneath' is the butcher's block ẖr with r, two strokes and the papyrus roll. The n after it is the genitive and is not needed in English. ḥꜣyt (the papyrus clump ḥꜣ, two reeds, t, a plant classifier; the clump and the plant are approximate) is some plant or thicket that cannot be pinned down (Budge: 'the flowers'). imy 'who is in' is the nisba of m: reed, the planks im, m and strokes. bꜣq (b, two vultures ꜣ, q and a tree) is the moringa, the tree that gives ben-oil (Budge: olive). The names make the speaker a being of the trees and thickets of the world below.

morph.gloss: to grow (verb)

sentences.l: pass · for-yourself · at-once · say · they · to · me
sentences.i: 'Pass on at once,' they say to me.
sentences.n: swꜣ is the imperative 'pass'. n·k (water n, basket ·k) is the dative 'for yourself' that often follows an imperative of motion. Budge prints swꜣ and n·k as one group; here they are two words. ḥr-ꜥ 'at once' is ḥr 'upon' (face and stroke) and ꜥ 'arm', literally 'on the arm'. The arm is written with the owl in front, as in m-ꜥ and nym. Budge prints the two parts as separate groups with the one gloss 'forthwith'; here they are joined as one word.

morph.gloss: say, said (verb; only after the words quoted: in·sn "they say")

sentences.l: passed · I · by · the-town · north · of-the-thicket
sentences.i: 'I have passed by the town north of the thicket.'
sentences.n: swꜣ·n·i 'I have passed' is the sḏm·n·f of swꜣ. niwt 'town' is the town sign with t and a stroke. mḥtt is spelled as on line 19; before a noun it is best taken as 'north (of)'. bꜣt 'bush, thicket' is b, two vultures ꜣ, t and a plant (approximate).

sentences.l: what · then · saw · you · there
sentences.i: 'What, then, did you see there?'
sentences.n: Budge prints pty tr as one group, 'What then'; here they are two words. pty 'what?' is stool p, t and two strokes y. tr is the knotted stalk alone with the man with his hand to his mouth. mꜣꜣ·n·k 'you saw' sets the eye and the sickle mꜣ in a ligature, then ꜣ, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k. im 'there' is the adverb (reed i, owl m). From here 'they say' is no longer written; question and answer simply alternate.

sentences.l: a-leg · it-is · and · a-thigh
sentences.i: 'It was a leg and a thigh.'
sentences.n: A sentence with pw: 'X pw' is 'it is X'. ḫnd (placenta ḫ, n, d, the leg and a flesh classifier, approximate) is read as 'leg, shin'. msdt (the fox-skins ms with s, d, t and the flesh classifier) is read as 'thigh'. Both readings follow the classifiers and Budge's 'leg' and 'thigh', but neither spelling is the usual one. ḥnꜥ 'and, with' is the twisted wick ḥ, n and arm ꜥ.

sentences.l: what · then · said · you · to · them
sentences.i: 'What, then, did you say to them?'
sentences.n: pty tr is split into two words as before. in·k 'you said' is taken as the verb in again, with ·k, as Budge takes it; but in is otherwise found only after the words quoted, not before them as here, and the group could also be ini 'bring', 'what did you bring them?'. Neither reading fits the answer well. n·sn 'to them' is the preposition n with the suffix ·sn; Budge prints them as two groups, joined here as one word.

morph.gloss: say, said (verb; in·k "you said")

sentences.l: saw · I · rejoicing · in · these · lands · of-the-Fenkhu
sentences.i: 'I saw rejoicing in these lands of the Fenkhu.'
sentences.n: iw (reed, quail chick) opens the statement and is not translated. mꜣꜣ·n·i 'I saw'. ihhy 'rejoicing, jubilation' is reed i with the man with his hand to his mouth (a cry), the courtyard h twice, two reeds and the same man again. nn 'these' (water n, the adze nw, the nw-pot and w, a fuller writing) is the demonstrative before its noun. tꜣw 'lands' is the land sign three times. fnḫw (horned viper f, n, ḫ, w) carries the classifiers of a foreign people: a cord sign, plural strokes, the throw-stick, a man and a woman. The Fenkhu are a people of Syria and the Levant coast. The answer does not obviously fit the question, but it is what the text gives.

morph.gloss: these, those (demonstrative, before its noun)
land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw "lands")

sentences.l: what · then · gave · they · to · you
sentences.i: 'What, then, did they give you?'
sentences.n: pty tr, split as before. rdit·sn 'they gave' is mouth r, the giving arm (printed without its loaf), t and ·sn. The t is unexpected: it may be the feminine of a relative form ('what is it that they gave') or a later spelling. n·k 'to you'.

sentences.l: a-flame · it-was · of · fire · together-with · a-papyrus-column(?) · of · faience
sentences.i: 'It was a flame of fire, together with a papyrus-column(?) of faience.'
sentences.n: bs (foot b, s, w and a flame on a stand, coded Q7, approximate) is taken as 'flame'. sḏt 'fire' is the crossed sticks, which also carry sḏ, with t and the flame; Budge reads it seśet. wꜣḏ is the papyrus stem with a cobra (wꜣḏ) and a small rectangle (coded Y5, approximate). It means a papyrus stem, the papyrus-shaped column or amulet, and something green; what object is meant here is not clear (Budge: 'tablet'). ṯḥnt 'faience, something gleaming' is the sign ṯḥn with n, t and three grains (Budge: 'crystal').

sentences.l: what · then · did · you · with · it
sentences.i: 'What, then, did you do with it?'
sentences.n: ir·n·k 'you did'. r·s 'with it' is r with ·s, here the bolt. The feminine 'it' may point to sḏt 'fire' or to the two things taken together.

sentences.l: buried · I · them · on · the-bank · of · Maati · as · things · of-the-night
sentences.i: 'I buried them on the bank of Maati, as things of the night.'
sentences.n: qrs 'bury' is q, r and s with a coffin (coded Q6) and the U15 sign, then n and ·i. st 'them, it' (bolt s, t) is the dependent pronoun of the 3rd person, here standing for the two things. wḏb 'riverbank, shore' is the sign wḏ (coded V24, approximate), b and land classifiers, the tongue of land wḏb (N20) and a canal sign (approximate). Budge's uteb has t, but the signs give ḏ. mꜣꜥti is written sickle, arm, t, two strokes and the plinth: Maati, the Two Truths, as in the name of the Hall. m ḫt ḫꜣwy is ḫt 'things' (placenta, t, papyrus roll) and ḫꜣwy 'evening, night' (the lotus-plant ḫꜣ (approximate) with ꜣ, w, y and the night sky). It might also be read m-ḫt ḫꜣwy 'after nightfall'. Budge has 'with the things of the night'.

morph.gloss: it, them (3rd person dependent pronoun, written s-t)
